claims.text: The target material is a Ta-based refractory high-entropy alloy with a BCC solid phase.
Near its melting point, the target alloy is a disordered liquid without pre-existing long-range order.
The proposed intervention trains an MLP on high-temperature liquid configurations generated by AIMD or DFT.
A liquid-state active-learning loop will correct deficiencies of standard EAM potentials in representing multicomponent liquid structure.
The MLP will replace ab initio potential-energy evaluations during the free-energy calculation.
The proposed free-energy calculation uses a thermodynamic cycle or coupling-parameter integration between reference and target states.
Chemical short-range order and local coordination in the liquid are critical to accurate free-energy estimation in multicomponent systems.
Liquid chemical fluctuations have diffuse-antiphase-boundary-like energy costs that the MLP must capture.
Standard EAM potentials fail in multicomponent liquids because they cannot represent the nonlinear dependence of energy on local chemical composition.
A machine-learning moment tensor potential has been used to simulate SRO-dependent behavior in solid MoNbTaW.
The MoNbTaW SRO study shows that an MLP can resolve the complex liquid chemical environments needed for melting free-energy calculations.
The failure mode of TOR-TILD or similar approaches is a sampling bottleneck caused by inadequate representation of high-entropy liquid disorder.
An inaccurate liquid potential can produce artificial ordering, incorrect coordination, and erroneous entropy and free-energy estimates along the integration path.
Local chemical clusters dominate the entropy and enthalpy of the multicomponent liquid.
The calculation should cover 0.9 Tm to 1.1 Tm at 1 atm with more than 100 ps of sampling per coupling-parameter window.
The MLP-based scheme will reduce computational cost by a factor of 10–100 relative to full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
The scheme will maintain accuracy within 5% for the melting point or free-energy difference.
The predicted melting point will be within 50 K of experiment or consistent with high-fidelity DFT benchmarks.
Standard TI with EAM or classical potentials typically produces melting-point errors greater than 100 K or incorrect phase stability in multicomponent alloys.
The proposed method may fail when the liquid has strong pre-melting order, the training set omits relevant configurations, or the reference and liquid states are too dissimilar.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says standard thermodynamic integration is replaced by a perturbation scheme, but the intervention still proposes thermodynamic integration along a coupling parameter. The text more clearly replaces ab initio energy evaluations than it replaces thermodynamic integration itself.

The baseline is defined as TI using EAM or other classical potentials, whereas the claimed 10–100× efficiency gain is measured against full ab initio TI. This leaves the primary cost comparator inconsistent.
